title: Your own assistant
snapshot: A snapshot, not a live feed. This page does not update itself.
lede: A plain look at a setup you could have. Your account. Your files. You can stop.
footer: Unified Solutions. This page explains a setup. It does not coach, and it does not hold client work.
have_intro: Four things you would actually feel. The rest is how we keep them true.

tiles.title: Your account
tiles.text: Your own sign-in. Not shared. You can stop anytime.

tiles.title: Your files
tiles.text: One folder for this assistant. A regular drawer, and a private drawer for sensitive files.

tiles.title: The models
tiles.text: A set amount each month, or a stronger model when the work needs it. Open can stay on the computer. Closed means a company runs it, and those words leave.

tiles.title: The work
tiles.text: Reports, invoices, draft emails, a watch on what you name. A business, or a personal life. You pick.

skills_intro: A plain list. No tool names.
can: Talk with you, and answer out loud.
Draft an email, a report, an invoice, or a page. You send it.
Watch the things you ask it to watch, and tell you when one is stuck.
Connect to email, a calendar, a spreadsheet, or Google Drive, if you say so.
Read a file you name. The read stays on the computer.
Learn how you like the work done, if you want it to. It does not quietly keep every sentence.
cannot: Send the email, post the page, or pay a bill unless you have said that kind of step is allowed.
Sit in a coaching session, or replace your judgment.
Open a sensitive file because it showed up nearby.
Quietly save every sentence, or keep a client name in memory.
Share your account, your files, or your keys.
Promise a company keeps nothing. That has not been confirmed.
Use a model hosted in China for names, scheduling, or private talk.
setup_intro: This is the shape. Your account is not someone else's login.

setup.title: Your account
setup.why: You own the sign-in. You can stop, or not use it, anytime.
points: Not a second login on someone else's account.
Turning it off is your call.

setup.title: Your folder
setup.why: One place, just for this assistant.
points: A regular drawer for everyday files.
A private drawer for anything sensitive.
You know where the finished work lands.

setup.title: The models
setup.why: We pick the model for the work. You do not have to know the names.
points: You can start with a set amount each month.
Open means it can run on the computer, so private words can stay here.
Closed means a company runs it, and those words leave the machine.

folders_intro: You should be able to point at the folder and know what belongs there.

folders.title: Everyday files
folders.why: Reports, drafts, and the work you asked for. This is where finished work lands.

folders.title: The private drawer
folders.why: Anything sensitive, or anything that needs care. It does not mix with the everyday files. The assistant can help you sort what goes here. It does not open a file because it is nearby.

folders.title: What it remembers
folders.why: How you like the work done, if you ask it to remember. Not every sentence. Not a client name.

folders.title: What it can connect
folders.why: Email, a calendar, a spreadsheet, Google Drive. Only the ones you choose. The rest stay off.

security_intro: Private, in plain words. A rule we keep. Not a locked room.

security.title: Your files stay in your folder
security.why: Sensitive files stay in the private drawer. A read you name stays on the computer.

security.title: Some words leave, on purpose
security.why: Ordinary questions can go to a company model. A spoken reply uses a speech service. A web question can go to a US company. We say that before we connect it.

security.title: It does not read what you did not hand it
security.why: Seeing a file is not permission to open it. The next file stays closed until you name it.

security.title: You can stop
security.why: Anytime. The account stays yours. Stopping is not a favor you have to ask for.

security.title: A company has not promised to keep nothing
security.why: We do not tell you they keep nothing. That has not been confirmed.

security.title: A model in China is not the backup
security.why: Used by hand, and only on text that is already public. It does not get names or private talk.

gift.intro: Same shape. Your own account. Your own files. You talk. You can stop. If a piece of this looks useful, say which piece. You do not have to take all of it.

required.title: Your own sign-in
required.text: Not shared. You can stop anytime.

required.title: A folder with a private drawer
required.text: Everyday files in one place. Sensitive files in another. You know where things land.

required.title: Models picked for the work
required.text: A set amount each month, or a stronger model when you need it. Open can stay on the computer. Closed means a company runs it, and those words leave.

required.title: Connect only what you want
required.text: Email, a calendar, a spreadsheet, Google Drive. The rest stay off.

required.title: It learns how you work, if you want that
required.text: You show it. You decide what it keeps. It does not quietly save every sentence.

easy: You do not learn a setup screen.
You can stop, or not use it, anytime.
not: Someone else's login, keys, or files.
A promise that a company keeps nothing.
A locked room that makes a mistake impossible.
The whole thing on day one. You can take the piece that is useful.

operator.intro: The nuts and bolts. You do not need this to understand the page.

facts.label: Everyday model
facts.value: grok-4.7. A company runs it. Ordinary work leaves this computer.

facts.label: Private model
facts.value: A smaller model on this computer. Private text stays here. It is not the strongest model.

facts.label: Speech
facts.value: What you say is turned into text on this computer. A spoken reply sends those words to a speech service.

facts.label: Search
facts.value: A question can go to a US company. Reading a public page starts here.

facts.label: Someone else's assistant
facts.value: A separate sign-in. Last check: up.

facts.label: Scheduled work
facts.value: 32 running, 3 paused, 35 in all. Job names are not on this page.

notes: The morning look, the weekly review, and the nightly backup are still running. A daily cost note is paused on purpose.
The private model fits the card in this computer. It keeps text here. It is not the strongest model.
Old conversations on this computer take a lot of space. Cleaning that up waits until the assistant is stopped. It is not done.
A software update is waiting. It was not applied for this snapshot.

limits.title: The backup path matches the written rule
limits.detail: At this snapshot, the extra stop was not on the parent chain. Ordinary failure goes to a US model, then to the small model on this computer.

limits.title: Do not say a company keeps nothing
limits.detail: By rule, private talk does not go to a company model. The company has not promised to keep nothing. The rule is ours. It is not their promise.

limits.title: Privacy is a rule we keep
limits.detail: It is not a locked room. A mistake is still possible. Disk encryption is still an open item.

limits.title: Folders are sorted by kind of work
limits.detail: Not one folder per business. Side work has landed in the practice folders. Do not describe it as a separate house for each venture.

limits.title: A hosted assistant shares the computer, not the keys
limits.detail: Separate sign-in, separate files, separate keys. Not a separate machine. Last check: up.

not_on_this_page: Client names, session content, and client files.
Other people's names, conversations, phone numbers, and files.
